steps.why: Room around the text helps reading.

steps.question: What should control corners say?
steps.why: Rounded corners feel friendly.
Caption is too faint for a label people must read.
Many readers are on phones.
Rounded corners match the warm reading tone. Sharp corners feel technical next to long text.

pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a warm tone, by brand convention. A rounded radius does this by curving the edge enough to feel soft, while the sides stay straight. So controls feel friendly next to long text and never compete with it, because the brand is warm (brand.q1), corners are rounded (shape.values) and each screen holds one idea (content.q2).

steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Only menus and dialogs float.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: Soft shadows suit warm paper.
The dimmed page focuses the reader on the dialog.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs in dark, in order to show height by tone,

on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So readers see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show their height as floating layers. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur in a 16% warm brown. So a menu lifts off warm paper without a hard edge, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).
darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light shadow's shape for menus and dialogs in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16% brown. So a menu still lifts off the dark page, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and dark ships for night reading (theming.values).

pick: radius.12: We use a 12px corner for article cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a warm tone by brand convention. A larger radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 8px controls inside it. So a card reads as one calm object on the page, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is warm (brand.q1).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line,

on surface.raised, beside the light shadow that does most of the lift. So readers see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
darkPick: neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line,

on surface.raised (#4A4339, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So readers see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed gets its own value for touch.
Moderate speed feels calm in a slow reading flow. A fast flash feels jumpy.
Keyboard users must always see where they are.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
darkPick: neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the canvas, for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets:
on surface.default and
on surface.raised, and
off the page. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads
on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
